llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Crawlora API helper for researching public Apple job postings, with manageable credential and external-service risks.

dimensions.detail: Outbound HTTPS requests to Crawlora and an API key are expected for the service integration, but users should understand that their search terms, job IDs, source metadata, and API key are sent to that provider.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install script, dependency installation, hook, service, or package mutation behavior was found; the package contains documentation, an endpoint reference, and one shell helper.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions clearly disclose use of CRAWLORA_API_KEY, curl, and api.crawlora.net, though the helper script still advertises generic Crawlora examples in comments that are not usable because the script restricts paths to Apple Jobs routes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence or privilege escalation behavior was found; the main residual issue is that the shell helper passes the API key to curl as a command-line header, which may expose it to local process inspection on some systems.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to search Apple Careers postings and fetch job details, and the artifact implements only the documented Crawlora Apple Jobs search and detail routes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using Crawlora as a third-party service for Apple job searches. Store CRAWLORA_API_KEY securely, avoid sending sensitive search terms unless intended, and prefer running the helper in an environment where other local users or processes cannot inspect command-line arguments.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell and network use are part of the documented helper workflow and are disclosed in the skill text; absence of a separate permission declaration is a review note, not evidence of hidden behavior.
[E1] expected: Transmission to api.crawlora.net is necessary for the Crawlora API workflow and is explicitly described in SKILL.md, reference/endpoints.md, and scripts/crawlora.sh.
[SQP-2] expected: The artifacts disclose the API key and external API use, but could warn more plainly that requests and credentials are transmitted to a third-party service.
[T09] unexpected: The API key is placed in curl's argument vector, creating a local credential-exposure risk; this is a hardening issue limited to the Crawlora credential rather than evidence of malicious intent.
